module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The Pompeiu problem

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{N+1}$ be a bounded domain. A **rigid motion** is an isometry of
$\mathbb{R}^{N+1}$ (a composition of translations and rotations), modelled here by an
`AffineIsometryEquiv` of Euclidean space with itself.

The domain $\Omega$ has the **Pompeiu property** if the only continuous function
$f : \mathbb{R}^{N+1} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $\int_{\sigma(\Omega)} f = 0$ for every rigid motion
$\sigma$ is $f \equiv 0$.

The **Pompeiu problem** (Pompeiu's conjecture) asserted that, among bounded simply connected
domains with Lipschitz boundary, the Euclidean ball is the *only* domain that **fails** to have
the Pompeiu property. That a ball fails is classical: radial functions built from Bessel
functions have vanishing integral over every congruent ball. The converse is false. Two
independent proofs of this negative conclusion are referenced below.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pompeiu_problem)
- [Encyclopedia of Mathematics](https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Pompeiu_problem)
- [BST73] Brown, L., Schreiber, B. M. and Taylor, B. A., *Spectral synthesis and the Pompeiu
  problem*, Ann. Inst. Fourier 23 (1973), 125–154. (Proves a ball fails the Pompeiu property;
  for a ball of radius `R` the witness is `f(x) = sin(a x₁)` with `J_{n/2}(a R) = 0`.)
- Zalcman, L., *A bibliographic survey of the Pompeiu problem*, in Approximation by
  Solutions of Partial Differential Equations, NATO ASI Ser. 365 (1992), 185–194.
- [CLD26] [Cao-Labora, G. and de Dios Pont, J., *Schiffer*](https://github.com/jaumededios/Schiffer),
  a Lean 4 formalization of a non-disk planar counterexample.
- [CS26] Colbrook, M. J. and Stepaniants, G., *A computer-assisted counterexample to the planar
  Pompeiu and Schiffer conjectures*, [arXiv:2608.01579](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01579) (2026).
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory Metric Topology

namespace PompeiuProblem

variable {N : ℕ}

/-- A **rigid motion** of $\mathbb{R}^{N+1}$: an affine isometry of Euclidean space onto itself
(a composition of translations and rotations/reflections). -/
abbrev RigidMotion (N : ℕ) :=
  AffineIsometryEquiv ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1))) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))

/-- A set `Ω` has the **Pompeiu property** if the only continuous `f : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ` whose integral
over every rigid-motion image `σ(Ω)` vanishes is the zero function. -/
def HasPompeiuProperty (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)) → ℝ, Continuous f →
    (∀ σ : RigidMotion N, (∫ x in Set.image σ Ω, f x) = 0) → ∀ x, f x = 0

/-- `Ω` is a **Euclidean ball**: an open metric ball of positive radius. -/
def IsBall (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (c : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1))) (r : ℝ), 0 < r ∧ Ω = Metric.ball c r

/-- `Ω` has **Lipschitz boundary** if every boundary point `p` has a neighbourhood `U` in which,
after some rigid motion `σ` (used to choose a "vertical" axis), `Ω` coincides with the strict
subgraph of a Lipschitz function `g` of the first `N` coordinates: a point `x ∈ U` lies in `Ω`
iff its last coordinate (in the `σ`-frame) is below `g` applied to its first `N` coordinates.
This is the standard definition of a Lipschitz domain. -/
def HasLipschitzBoundary (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ frontier Ω, ∃ (U : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))),
    U ∈ 𝓝 p ∧ ∃ (σ : RigidMotion N) (K : NNReal) (g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) → ℝ),
      LipschitzWith K g ∧
        ∀ x ∈ U, x ∈ Ω ↔ (σ x) (Fin.last N) <
          g ((WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin N → ℝ)).symm (fun i : Fin N => (σ x) i.castSucc))

/-- The domain hypotheses of Pompeiu's problem: `Ω` is bounded, open, connected (a "domain"),
simply connected, and has Lipschitz boundary. -/
structure IsAdmissibleDomain (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) : Prop where
  bounded            : Bornology.IsBounded Ω
  isOpen             : IsOpen Ω
  connected          : IsConnected Ω
  simplyConnected    : SimplyConnectedSpace Ω
  lipschitzBoundary  : HasLipschitzBoundary Ω

/--
**Pompeiu's conjecture is false.** There is a bounded, simply connected Lipschitz domain in
$\mathbb{R}^2$ which fails to have the Pompeiu property but is not a Euclidean ball. This conclusion
has two independent proofs: the Lean-formalized construction of Cao-Labora and de Dios Pont
[CLD26], and the computer-assisted construction of Colbrook and Stepaniants [CS26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 42,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/jaumededios/Schiffer/blob/2938e277969c329caf154e48a3d8823f3635c7f1/Schiffer/FormalConjecturesSolution.lean#L446-L469"]
theorem pompeiu_conjecture :
    ¬ ∀ (N : ℕ) (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))),
      IsAdmissibleDomain Ω → (¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω ↔ IsBall Ω) := by
  sorry

/--
The classical (easy) direction, proved by Brown–Schreiber–Taylor [BST73]: a Euclidean ball fails
to have the Pompeiu property. For a ball of radius `R`, an explicit witness is `f(x) = sin(a x₁)`
where `a > 0` is chosen so that the Bessel function `J_{n/2}(a R) = 0`; its integral over every
congruent ball vanishes.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 42]
theorem ball_not_hasPompeiuProperty (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1))))
    (hball : IsBall Ω) :
    ¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω := by
  sorry

/--
The hard direction of the Pompeiu problem is false: some admissible planar domain lacks the
Pompeiu property without being a ball. Two independent proofs are given in [CLD26] and [CS26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 42,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/jaumededios/Schiffer/blob/2938e277969c329caf154e48a3d8823f3635c7f1/Schiffer/FormalConjecturesSolution.lean#L446-L469"]
theorem not_hasPompeiuProperty_imp_ball :
    ¬ ∀ (N : ℕ) (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))),
      IsAdmissibleDomain Ω → ¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω → IsBall Ω := by
  sorry

/-- Sanity check: the zero function always integrates to `0` over every rigid-motion image, so the
hypothesis in `HasPompeiuProperty` is satisfiable (the property is not vacuously false). -/
@[category test, AMS 42]
theorem integral_zero_eq_zero (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) (σ : RigidMotion N) :
    (∫ _x in Set.image σ Ω, (0 : ℝ)) = 0 := by
  simp

end PompeiuProblem

findings.description:
The theorem negates `∀ (N : ℕ) (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))), IsAdmissibleDomain Ω → (¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω ↔ IsBall Ω)`. That is Pompeiu's conjecture in every dimension N+1, and `IsAdmissibleDomain` has `SimplyConnectedSpace Ω` as its only topological hypothesis. In dimension ≥ 3, simple connectivity does not exclude spherical shells, the standard trivial non-Pompeiu domains. So the universal claim inside `¬` is false for elementary classical reasons, and the theorem holds whether or not a planar counterexample exists.

Witness at N = 2: Ω = {x ∈ ℝ³ : 1 < ‖x‖ < 2}.
- Admissible: it is bounded, open and connected. It is simply connected, since Ω ≅ S² × (1,2) and π₁(S²) = 0. Its frontier is two spheres. After a rotation sending a boundary point to a pole, Ω is locally the strict subgraph of a truncated ±√(1−|x'|²) or √(4−|x'|²), so `HasLipschitzBoundary` holds.
- Not a ball: it is not convex.
- Fails `HasPompeiuProperty`: its indicator has radial Fourier transform χ̂(ξ) = (4π/s)∫₁² r sin(rs) dr = 4π·h(s)/s³, with s = ‖ξ‖ and h(s) = sin 2s − sin s − s(2cos 2s − cos s). Since h(π/2) = π − 1 > 0 > h(2π) = −2π, h has a root s₀ ≈ 2.0146; I confirmed the root and the radial integral numerically. For f x = cos(s₀·x 0), which is continuous with f 0 = 1, and any σ x = Qx + b, ∫_{σ''Ω} f = Re(e^{i s₀ b₀}·χ̂(−s₀Qᵀe₀)) = 0.

So the Lean statement is true without the 2026 planar counterexample and would stay true even if the planar conjecture held. It does not state what its docstring and sources claim: a bounded simply connected Lipschitz non-disc in ℝ² that fails the Pompeiu property. The root cause is `IsAdmissibleDomain.simplyConnected` combined with quantifying over all N. In ℝⁿ the problem is posed for connected boundary or connected exterior; in the plane that is what simple connectivity gives. The file's local history shows the same issue earlier: the open version (#4436) was already classically false at N = 2.
findings.source_evidence: Colbrook–Stepaniants, arXiv:2608.01579 (cited as [CS26]), §1: "The planar Pompeiu conjecture for bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains asserts that a domain in this class can fail this property only if it is a disc. ... We disprove both statements." Its abstract: "We construct a bounded simply connected noncircular domain Ω⊂ℝ² ... a counterexample to the planar Pompeiu conjecture for bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains." Cao-Labora–de Dios Pont, arXiv:2608.05114: "We disprove both conjectures in ℝ²". Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pompeiu_problem): "a counterexample in two dimensions to the Pompeiu and Schiffer problems". The n-dimensional problem as posed elsewhere: the Szeged page linked from Wikipedia (https://www.math.u-szeged.hu/~odor/pompeiu.htm) says "then the domain is a ball, provided K is 'nice' - that is bounded and it admits connected Lipschitzian boundary"; EoM (https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Pompeiu_problem) says "Ω is a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary ... such that ℝⁿ∖Ω̄ is connected". Both exclude shells. The theorem's own docstring: "There is a bounded, simply connected Lipschitz domain in ℝ² which fails to have the Pompeiu property but is not a Euclidean ball."
findings.suggested_fix: State the planar claim, as the docstring and CS26 do: `theorem pompeiu_conjecture : ¬ ∀ Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), IsAdmissibleDomain (N := 1) Ω → (¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω ↔ IsBall Ω)`. This typechecks against the file's definitions. The external proof already instantiates `N = 1` (`hconjecture 1 …`). Alternatively, for an all-dimensional statement, add a hypothesis to `IsAdmissibleDomain` that excludes shells, e.g. `IsConnected (closure Ω)ᶜ` (EoM) or a connected `frontier Ω` (Szeged page).

findings.description: This has the same defect as `pompeiu_conjecture`. `¬ ∀ (N : ℕ) (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))), IsAdmissibleDomain Ω → ¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω → IsBall Ω` is witnessed at N = 2 by the classical shell {1 < ‖x‖ < 2} ⊂ ℝ³. The shell is bounded, open, connected, simply connected (≅ S² × (1,2)), has smooth hence Lipschitz boundary, and is not a ball. It fails the Pompeiu property: its indicator's radial Fourier transform vanishes on the sphere ‖ξ‖ = s₀ ≈ 2.0146, where h(s₀) = 0 for h(s) = sin 2s − sin s − s(2cos 2s − cos s), so cos(s₀·x 0) integrates to 0 over every isometric copy. The docstring says "some admissible planar domain lacks the Pompeiu property without being a ball", but the Lean does not fix the plane. As stated, the theorem is an elementary pre-2026 fact, not the planar disproof it is tagged and `formal_proof`-linked as. The external challenge file (jaumededios/Schiffer, `FormalConjecturesChallenge.lean`) copies this statement verbatim, so that challenge could be met with the 3-D shell.
findings.source_evidence: CS26 (arXiv:2608.01579), §1: "The planar Pompeiu conjecture for bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains asserts that a domain in this class can fail this property only if it is a disc. ... We disprove both statements." CLD26 (arXiv:2608.05114), abstract: "We disprove both conjectures in ℝ²". The higher-dimensional problem requires "connected Lipschitzian boundary" (https://www.math.u-szeged.hu/~odor/pompeiu.htm) or "ℝⁿ∖Ω̄ connected" (https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Pompeiu_problem). The declaration's docstring: "some admissible planar domain lacks the Pompeiu property without being a ball".
findings.suggested_fix: `theorem not_hasPompeiuProperty_imp_ball : ¬ ∀ Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), IsAdmissibleDomain (N := 1) Ω → ¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω → IsBall Ω`. This typechecks, implies the current statement via `fun H => h (H 1)`, and is exactly what the external proof establishes. Alternatively, strengthen `IsAdmissibleDomain` with `IsConnected (closure Ω)ᶜ` (or a connected frontier) if an all-dimensional form is wanted.

findings.description: The docstring calls the ball direction "The classical (easy) direction, proved by Brown–Schreiber–Taylor [BST73]". The module docstring's BST73 entry likewise says "(Proves a ball fails the Pompeiu property; ...)". The cited source CLD26 credits this fact to Chakalov (1944), decades before BST73. BST73's own abstract presents its contribution as a Fourier–Laplace characterization of property (P) in ℝ², plus proofs that many planar regions *have* the property. The mathematics, including the Bessel witness sin(a x₁) with J_{n/2}(aR) = 0, is correct; only the attribution is off.
findings.source_evidence: Cao-Labora–de Dios Pont, arXiv:2608.05114, §1: "It was pointed out by Chakalov [L. Chakalov, Sur un problème de D. Pompeiu, Annuaire Univ. Sofia 40 (1944), 1–14] that the answer is negative if Ω is a ball. In 1976, Williams proved ... Williams' proof builds on previous work of Brown, Schreiber and Taylor." BST73 abstract (http://www.numdam.org/item/AIF_1973__23_3_125_0/): "As an application of the above result a characterization of such measures is obtained in terms of their Fourier-Laplace transforms ... it is shown that property (P) is satisfied by the area measures on a large class of compact regions in the plane."
findings.suggested_fix: Attribute the ball case to Chakalov (1944) as classical, e.g. "The classical direction (Chakalov 1944; see also [BST73])", and adjust the BST73 reference note accordingly.

reformulations.difference: Rigid motions are all of `AffineIsometryEquiv` (reflections included) and the test functions f are real-valued. EoM uses the orientation-preserving group M(n); CS26 uses complex-valued f, though its rigid motions σ(x) = Qx + b already allow Q ∈ O(2). The module docstring says "translations and rotations", while the `RigidMotion` docstring correctly says rotations/reflections.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Real vs complex f: if a complex f ≠ 0 has all integrals zero, so do Re f and Im f, and one of them is nonzero; a real f is a complex f. Full group vs M(n): the Pompeiu property for M(n) implies it for the full group, because the hypothesis over the larger group is stronger. Conversely, if a bounded Ω fails for M(n), then by Brown–Schreiber–Taylor χ̂_Ω vanishes on a quadric {ζ·ζ = α}, α ≠ 0. That quadric is O(n,ℂ)-invariant, so Re or Im of e^{iζ·x} integrates to 0 over every isometric copy, mirror images included. For the Schiffer-type counterexamples, Green's identity gives this directly, since Helmholtz solutions are invariant under all isometries. In ℝ¹ the admissible sets are intervals, and sin(2πx/L) works for translations and reflections alike.

reformulations.difference: The disproof is phrased as `¬ ∀ …, IsAdmissibleDomain Ω → (¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω ↔ IsBall Ω)`. The negated iff formally also allows an admissible ball that has the Pompeiu property, rather than directly asserting an admissible non-ball that fails it.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The extra disjunct (a ball with the Pompeiu property) is excluded by `ball_not_hasPompeiuProperty`. So the statement is equivalent to `not_hasPompeiuProperty_imp_ball`. I proved both implications in a scratch file; the reverse direction takes the ball statement as a hypothesis. This concerns the internal form only and does not affect the dimension defect reported in the findings.

sources_consulted: http://www.numdam.org/item/AIF_1973__23_3_125_0/ (BST73 abstract and reference list; the PDF is a scanned image without a text layer)
jaumededios/Schiffer @2938e27: Schiffer/FormalConjecturesChallenge.lean, Schiffer/Statement.lean, README.md, formalization.yaml (codeload tarball)
could_not_verify: PompeiuProblem.pompeiu_conjecture / PompeiuProblem.not_hasPompeiuProperty_imp_ball (`formal_proof` link): the linked external theorem at L446–469 has definitions and a statement identical to this file's, and it implies `pompeiu_conjecture` by a one-line argument (checked in Lean). A source scan of the repository at 2938e27 finds `sorry` only in the two challenge files, which the solution does not import, and no `axiom` declarations; formalization.yaml reports a full build with only propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice. I did not build the external project (Lean v4.29.0, separate Mathlib) or run `#print axioms` myself.

PompeiuProblem.ball_not_hasPompeiuProperty (attribution only): BST73's Numdam PDF is a scanned image, so I could not check whether BST73 itself states or proves the ball case. The minor finding rests on CLD26's attribution to Chakalov (1944) and on the BST73 abstract.
review.notes:
The main defect is the combination of quantifying over every dimension (`∀ N`) with `SimplyConnectedSpace` as the only topological hypothesis in `IsAdmissibleDomain`. In ℝ² this matches the source class (CS26: bounded simply connected Lipschitz domains). In ℝ³ and above, spherical shells are simply connected, have Lipschitz boundary, are not balls, and trivially fail the Pompeiu property. So `¬ ∀ N …` holds for classical reasons and does not certify the 2026 planar result. The file's history shows the same gap earlier: the open version introduced in #4436 was already refutable at N = 2, and #4712 only wrapped it in `¬ ∀ N` and retagged it solved. Restricting both theorems to `Fin 2` (N = 1) fixes this; it typechecks, and the external proof already works at N = 1.

Everything else checks out:
- `HasLipschitzBoundary` is the standard strong-Lipschitz local-subgraph definition. It correctly rules out punctured balls and slits.
- `IsBall`, with exact equality to an open ball, is fine for open Lipschitz domains.
- Integrals over bounded images of continuous functions carry no junk values.
- The N = 0 case is consistent: admissible sets in ℝ¹ are intervals, all of which are balls and fail the property.
- Status `research solved` agrees with CS26 (3 Aug 2026), CLD26 (5 Aug 2026, Lean-verified) and Wikipedia.

Harmless docstring nits:
- `integral_zero_eq_zero` says \"not vacuously false\"; the relevant worry would be vacuous truth, and f = 0 also satisfies the conclusion.
- The module docstring describes rigid motions as translations and rotations, but `AffineIsometryEquiv` includes reflections.
- CLD26 also has an arXiv preprint (2608.05114) that could be cited next to the GitHub repo.

not_demonstrated.reason: The statement is true, and its witness (the 3-D spherical shell) needs real mathematics to verify in Lean. Simple connectivity needs π₁(S²) = 0, which Mathlib lacks. Lipschitz boundary needs explicit charts. Failure of the Pompeiu property needs a Fourier/spherical integral computation over all isometric images plus a root of h(s) = sin 2s − sin s − s(2cos 2s − cos s). The definitions offer no degenerate shortcut.

Same witness and the same obstacles as `pompeiu_conjecture`. The statement is true for classical reasons at N = 2, but formalizing that requires π₁(S²) = 0, explicit Lipschitz charts for two spheres, and an explicit Fourier computation for the shell's indicator, none of which is a few-line proof.

submission.summary: No trivial proof file was produced. Both flagged theorems are true as stated but weaker than the planar claim. The only elementary witness (a spherical shell in ℝ³, which is simply connected, has Lipschitz boundary, is not a ball and fails the Pompeiu property) needs substantial topology and analysis that Mathlib does not supply, e.g. π₁(S²) = 0. The definitions contain no degenerate shortcut, so the findings stand on the mathematical argument given in the review.
submission.gave_up_reason: Both reported statements (`PompeiuProblem.pompeiu_conjecture` and `PompeiuProblem.not_hasPompeiuProperty_imp_ball`) are TRUE as stated. The defect is that they are weaker than the source's claim, provable from a classical 3-D example rather than the 2026 planar counterexample. So there is no small counterexample to compute. A demonstration must exhibit an explicit admissible non-ball Ω that fails `HasPompeiuProperty`, and the definitions leave no degenerate shortcut. Admissible sets are nonempty, open and bounded, hence of positive measure. Integrals of continuous functions over their rigid-motion images are genuine, never Lean's default 0. In ℝ¹ (N = 0) every admissible set is an interval, i.e. a ball. The only elementary witness is the spherical shell {1 < ‖x‖ < 2} ⊂ ℝ³. Showing it is simply connected needs π₁(S²) = 0, which is absent from Mathlib (only `SimplyConnectedSpace.ofContractible` exists, and the shell is not contractible). `HasLipschitzBoundary` needs explicit rotation/reflection charts and truncated square roots. Failing the Pompeiu property needs a spherical-coordinates Fourier computation of ∫ cos(s₀x₀) over every isometric image, plus an intermediate-value root of h. That is real mathematics, far beyond a few lines. No file was created.

not_fixed.reason: Only the minor attribution slip was reported here: the ball fact is credited to BST73, while CLD26 credits Chakalov (1944). The mathematics is correct. My confidence was low (0.3) and I could not read BST73 itself (scanned PDF), so changing the attribution did not seem trivially safe. Left unchanged.

submission.summary:
Restricted both solved theorems to the plane. They now quantify over `Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))`, with `N = 1` inferred. This matches their own docstrings ("in ℝ²", "planar") and CS26/CLD26. The old all-dimensional forms were true for a classical reason (3-D spherical shells are simply connected, Lipschitz, not balls, and trivially fail the Pompeiu property).

Consequential docstring edits:
- Module docstring: the conjecture is now described as planar, with a note on why. In dimension ≥ 3, simple connectivity admits spherical shells, and the higher-dimensional problem is posed for connected boundary or exterior.
- `IsAdmissibleDomain`: docstring now says these are the planar hypotheses, used with `N = 1`. The definition is unchanged.

Unchanged: the definitions, `ball_not_hasPompeiuProperty`, the categories, AMS tags and `formal_proof` attributes.

Checked on a compiled copy of the edited file:
- Each new statement implies the old one (`fun h H => h (H 1)`).
- Given `ball_not_hasPompeiuProperty`, the two new statements are equivalent.
- The file compiles with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.

Caveat for maintainers: the kept `formal_proof` link (jaumededios/Schiffer, FormalConjecturesSolution.lean L446–469) points to a declaration stated for all dimensions. Its proof applies the hypothesis only at `N = 1` (`hconjecture 1 …`), so it proves the planar statement once the `1` is dropped. Literally, though, its declared type is the old weaker statement. The external challenge and solution files should be updated to the planar form and the link refreshed. That change is outside this repository.

/-!
# The Pompeiu problem

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{N+1}$ be a bounded domain. A **rigid motion** is an isometry of
$\mathbb{R}^{N+1}$ (a composition of translations and rotations), modelled here by an
`AffineIsometryEquiv` of Euclidean space with itself.

The domain $\Omega$ has the **Pompeiu property** if the only continuous function
$f : \mathbb{R}^{N+1} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $\int_{\sigma(\Omega)} f = 0$ for every rigid motion
$\sigma$ is $f \equiv 0$.

The **Pompeiu problem** (Pompeiu's conjecture) asserted that, among bounded simply connected
planar domains with Lipschitz boundary, the disc is the *only* domain that **fails** to have
the Pompeiu property. That a ball fails is classical, in every dimension: radial functions built
from Bessel functions have vanishing integral over every congruent ball. The converse is false.
Two independent proofs of this negative conclusion are referenced below.

The conjecture is therefore stated in the plane ($N = 1$). For $N \ge 2$, simple connectivity does
not exclude spherical shells $\{1 < \|x\| < 2\}$, which fail the Pompeiu property for elementary
reasons: the Fourier transform of their indicator is radial and vanishes on a sphere. In higher
dimensions the problem is posed for domains whose boundary (or exterior) is connected.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pompeiu_problem)
- [Encyclopedia of Mathematics](https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Pompeiu_problem)
- [BST73] Brown, L., Schreiber, B. M. and Taylor, B. A., *Spectral synthesis and the Pompeiu
  problem*, Ann. Inst. Fourier 23 (1973), 125–154. (Proves a ball fails the Pompeiu property;
  for a ball of radius `R` the witness is `f(x) = sin(a x₁)` with `J_{n/2}(a R) = 0`.)
- Zalcman, L., *A bibliographic survey of the Pompeiu problem*, in Approximation by
  Solutions of Partial Differential Equations, NATO ASI Ser. 365 (1992), 185–194.
- [CLD26] [Cao-Labora, G. and de Dios Pont, J., *Schiffer*](https://github.com/jaumededios/Schiffer),
  a Lean 4 formalization of a non-disk planar counterexample.
- [CS26] Colbrook, M. J. and Stepaniants, G., *A computer-assisted counterexample to the planar
  Pompeiu and Schiffer conjectures*, [arXiv:2608.01579](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01579) (2026).
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory Metric Topology

namespace PompeiuProblem

variable {N : ℕ}

/-- A **rigid motion** of $\mathbb{R}^{N+1}$: an affine isometry of Euclidean space onto itself
(a composition of translations and rotations/reflections). -/
abbrev RigidMotion (N : ℕ) :=
  AffineIsometryEquiv ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1))) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))

/-- A set `Ω` has the **Pompeiu property** if the only continuous `f : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ` whose integral
over every rigid-motion image `σ(Ω)` vanishes is the zero function. -/
def HasPompeiuProperty (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)) → ℝ, Continuous f →
    (∀ σ : RigidMotion N, (∫ x in Set.image σ Ω, f x) = 0) → ∀ x, f x = 0

/-- `Ω` is a **Euclidean ball**: an open metric ball of positive radius. -/
def IsBall (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (c : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1))) (r : ℝ), 0 < r ∧ Ω = Metric.ball c r

/-- `Ω` has **Lipschitz boundary** if every boundary point `p` has a neighbourhood `U` in which,
after some rigid motion `σ` (used to choose a "vertical" axis), `Ω` coincides with the strict
subgraph of a Lipschitz function `g` of the first `N` coordinates: a point `x ∈ U` lies in `Ω`
iff its last coordinate (in the `σ`-frame) is below `g` applied to its first `N` coordinates.
This is the standard definition of a Lipschitz domain. -/
def HasLipschitzBoundary (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ frontier Ω, ∃ (U : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))),
    U ∈ 𝓝 p ∧ ∃ (σ : RigidMotion N) (K : NNReal) (g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) → ℝ),
      LipschitzWith K g ∧
        ∀ x ∈ U, x ∈ Ω ↔ (σ x) (Fin.last N) <
          g ((WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin N → ℝ)).symm (fun i : Fin N => (σ x) i.castSucc))

/-- The domain hypotheses of the planar Pompeiu problem (used with `N = 1`): `Ω` is bounded, open,
connected (a "domain"), simply connected, and has Lipschitz boundary. -/
structure IsAdmissibleDomain (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) : Prop where
  bounded            : Bornology.IsBounded Ω
  isOpen             : IsOpen Ω
  connected          : IsConnected Ω
  simplyConnected    : SimplyConnectedSpace Ω
  lipschitzBoundary  : HasLipschitzBoundary Ω

/--
**Pompeiu's conjecture is false.** There is a bounded, simply connected Lipschitz domain in
$\mathbb{R}^2$ which fails to have the Pompeiu property but is not a Euclidean ball. This conclusion
has two independent proofs: the Lean-formalized construction of Cao-Labora and de Dios Pont
[CLD26], and the computer-assisted construction of Colbrook and Stepaniants [CS26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 42,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/jaumededios/Schiffer/blob/2938e277969c329caf154e48a3d8823f3635c7f1/Schiffer/FormalConjecturesSolution.lean#L446-L469"]
theorem pompeiu_conjecture :
    ¬ ∀ Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
      IsAdmissibleDomain Ω → (¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω ↔ IsBall Ω) := by
  sorry

/--
The classical (easy) direction, proved by Brown–Schreiber–Taylor [BST73]: a Euclidean ball fails
to have the Pompeiu property. For a ball of radius `R`, an explicit witness is `f(x) = sin(a x₁)`
where `a > 0` is chosen so that the Bessel function `J_{n/2}(a R) = 0`; its integral over every
congruent ball vanishes.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 42]
theorem ball_not_hasPompeiuProperty (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1))))
    (hball : IsBall Ω) :
    ¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω := by
  sorry

/--
The hard direction of the Pompeiu problem is false: some admissible planar domain lacks the
Pompeiu property without being a ball. Two independent proofs are given in [CLD26] and [CS26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 42,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/jaumededios/Schiffer/blob/2938e277969c329caf154e48a3d8823f3635c7f1/Schiffer/FormalConjecturesSolution.lean#L446-L469"]
theorem not_hasPompeiuProperty_imp_ball :
    ¬ ∀ Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
      IsAdmissibleDomain Ω → ¬ HasPompeiuProperty Ω → IsBall Ω := by
  sorry

/-- Sanity check: the zero function always integrates to `0` over every rigid-motion image, so the
hypothesis in `HasPompeiuProperty` is satisfiable (the property is not vacuously false). -/
@[category test, AMS 42]
theorem integral_zero_eq_zero (Ω : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N + 1)))) (σ : RigidMotion N) :
    (∫ _x in Set.image σ Ω, (0 : ℝ)) = 0 := by
  simp

end PompeiuProblem
